name: High Fives Dominoes
description: High Fives Dominoes is a western domino connecting game played with a double-15 set, using the extended value range to create longer sessions and more complex end control. Players match open ends while managing mobility and high-value risk, since high numbers can amplify blocking and pip exposure outcomes.

history.origins: High Fives Dominoes is encountered as a modern extended-set format that relies on large western domino sets for long sessions and larger groups.
timeline: Modern era: extended domino sets become widely available and used for specialized formats.
history.cultural: Played socially as a longer session game where mobility planning and defensive safety are rewarded.
history.evolution: The larger set increases the value range, making end-control and blocking more complex and high-number exposure more consequential.

setup.dealing: Deal tiles by player count; remaining tiles form a boneyard if the profile uses draws.
setup.equipment: Domino set and optional score tracking by match profile.

rules.objective: Play legal matching tiles and end hands with the best score under the match profile.
rules.gameplay: Players place a legal tile to a matching open end of the shared layout. When blocked, the match profile determines whether to draw from a boneyard or pass. Hands end when a player empties their hand or play is blocked, and scoring follows the profile in use.
keyRules: A played tile must match the value of an exposed open end.
Blocked turns are resolved by draw-or-pass profile rules.
Hand-end and scoring depend on the match profile.

strategy.basic: Keep connectors that cover multiple values and avoid holding high-number tiles too long.
strategy.intermediate: Track which high values have appeared so you do not open values you cannot reliably answer.
strategy.advanced: Shape open ends to pressure opponents while keeping safe exits across the broad range of values.
tips: Do not expose a high value unless you can keep responding to it.
Preserve mid-range flexibility to avoid being forced into a single dangerous value.
